messages:
maggie: quick heads-up — flipped FP8 on staging for the mixed-precision stack. Observed ~8–12% token/sec improvement but a ~1.7% ROUGE-L drop on the summarization calibration set. wondering if dataset skew or kernel fallback is the culprit.

dan: do we have profiler traces? did kernel selection change for attention or feed-forward?

sahil: i uploaded an initial perf dump a few mins ago. quick read: we see some fallback to int8 kernels for attention on a subset of requests; those correlate with latency spikes.

okeefe: can you paste the profiler snippet here? also, are we running per-channel or per-tensor calibration? that choice can change outlier sensitivity a lot.

maggie: profiler attached via comp-bot below. we're currently using per-tensor (legacy path). sample set = "long-tail-aug": ~3k examples, heavy on long contexts and multi-turn snippets.

comp-bot: PROFILER OUTPUT
```
TIMELINE: steps 120-180
kernel_choice: fp8_gemm_v2 (60%), int8_attention_fallback (40%)
kv_cache_warmup: median 7 steps to stable
avg_latency_per_token: baseline 18.0ms -> fp8 15.8ms
io_wait: 2.3ms spikes during warmup on fallback requests
````

dan: int8_attention_fallback is the red flag — sounds like quantization error triggered fallback to a conservative kernel. per-tensor scales can’t capture per-head variance in activations, so one head's outliers can wreck the global scale.

sahil: agreed. also the calibration corpus skew (long contexts) probably under-samples typical short-context activations, so scales are tuned for tail distributions and hurt normal-case quality. plus KV cache warmup interplay: early tokens have different distributions.

okeefe: proposal: two-pass calibration run. 1) per-channel on a short-context subset (e.g., first 256 tokens) to stabilize head-wise scales. 2) full-pass on long-context subset with clipping for outliers. also add runtime flag: enable_hotkey_kernel_hysteresis=true to avoid flip-flopping kernels on transient signals.

maggie: can we A/B per-channel vs per-tensor on a 200-sample holdout? isolate whether kernel-switch triggers are dataset-driven.

dan: will run two experiments: per-tensor vs per-channel. both seeded and with controlled batch sizes (no dynamic batching) — results in ~30m.

sahil: instrumenting runtime to log (lightweight) which layer/head forced fallback + KV cache hit rate per request. counter aggregation per 1k req should be fine.

okeefe: also check batching heuristics during calibration runs — if batch sizes or seq-len distribution vary mid-run we might trigger non-optimal kernel selection. prefer fixed batch/profile windows for calibration.

maggie: noted. thanks team :thumbsup:

comp-bot: EXPERIMENT CREATED -> /tasks/2345 run-perchannel-vs-pertensor --samples 200 --seed 42 --notes "kv-warmup-instrument"

dan: quick summary of experiment results: per-channel -> no attention fallbacks observed, +1.9% ROUGE, +7% throughput. per-tensor -> fallbacks in ~12% of requests, -1.6% ROUGE, +10% raw throughput but high variance and occasional latency regressions.

sahil: interesting: per-channel preserves quality and stabilizes kernel selection; it sacrifices a bit of peak throughput but is more predictable for SLOs.

okeefe: actionable heuristic: adopt per-channel for FP8 in dedicated/alpha where quality matters. implement outlier-percentile clipping: compute per-head 99.9th percentile during calibration and cap scales to avoid explosive quant factors from tiny counts.

maggie: next actions: 1) default per-channel for FP8 in Dedicated alpha, 2) add outlier clipping (99.9p) to calibration pipeline, 3) bake KV-warmup and kernel-hyst instrumentation into runtime, 4) update docs with calibration dataset recipe (stratified short+long contexts, head-token frequency buckets).

dan: PR for instrumentation + experiment harness incoming.

sahil: i'll draft a calibration runbook with sampling recipes and recommended batch/window sizes.

okeefe: add a small canary with kernel-hysteresis so a single-request blip can't flip kernels globally.

maggie: agreed — follow up once PRs land and metrics look good. closing loop soon :sparkles:
